title: Which counting method is best for a large herd?
description: Sticks, letters and Roman symbols are compared on two tests: does the sequence ever end, and is it convenient for counting a large collection? Keeko's doubt is that letters are the best way because they are quick to say.
teaching_notes: One idea: a good number system must be an unending standard sequence that is also convenient to count with, and each method meets only one of these. Watch for students who judge a method on speed alone and forget to ask whether it ever ends.

source: Compare the three counting methods (sticks, letters a to z,
video_script.why: The child sees the challenge behind every number system: the sequence must never end and must also be convenient to count with.
video_script.substitution: Put the three methods in a table and ask the same two questions of each one.
video_script.anchor: a table with three rows, sticks, letters and Roman symbols, and two columns, never ends and convenient to count with
video_script.wrong_answer: letters are the best way because they are quick to say
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says letters are the best way because they are quick to say. After z there is no next letter, so letters stop at twenty six cows.
video_script.payoff_line: None of the three is both unending and convenient to count with

final_answer.value: Sticks never end but are slow; letters are quick but end at 26; Roman symbols need ever new symbols
final_answer.spoken: sticks never end but are slow, letters are quick but end at twenty six, and Roman symbols need ever new symbols

hold_back: Sticks never end but are slow; letters are quick but end at 26; Roman symbols need ever new symbols
never_show: the answer card before the last beat of the board solution
maths_rules: a number system is a standard sequence of objects, names or symbols in a fixed order
sticks: one more stick can always be added, so the sequence never ends; a collection needs as many sticks as objects
letters: quick to say, but the alphabet has 26 letters, so the sequence ends at z
Roman symbols: convenient, but bigger numbers keep needing new symbols
the challenge: an unending standard sequence that is convenient to count with
video_script.design: One idea: ask the same two questions of all three methods. The table stays on the stage and one row fills at each step.
